title: A line chart's geometry
hints: Compute ticks as `k × step` for whole numbers `k` from `floor(lo / step)` to `ceil(hi / step)`: adding `step` repeatedly would give values like `0.30000000000000004`.
For the nearest point, `std::lower_bound` finds the first point with `x >= target`; the answer is either it or the point before it.

The perpendicular distance of `p` from the line through `a` and `b` is `|(b.x - a.x)(a.y - p.y) - (a.x - p.x)(b.y - a.y)| / length(b - a)`, the cross product divided by the line's length; when `a` and `b` are the same point, use the plain distance from `p` to `a`.
requirements: Axis ticks are round numbers covering the data, for any range and scale.
Data and screen coordinates convert both ways, with y flipped.
The tooltip point is found by binary search, with ties going to the lower index.
Simplification keeps the shape within the tolerance and removes collinear points.
stretch: Add a second series with its own colour, a legend, and time on the x axis with ticks at round dates (whole hours, days or months, depending on the range).
